Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 31889 of 2023

Applicant :- Vikas Viswakarma
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- R.K.Paramhans Singh,Manvendra Narain Pathak
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri R.K. Paramhans, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned Brief Holder for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 193 of 2023, under Sections 354, 506, 376 IPC and Section 67 I.T. Act, Police Station Kotwali,
District Deoria during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant under Section 354, 506 IPC and according to the FIR applicant used to harass the daughter of the informant aged about 18 years.
4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that admittedly prosecutrix of the case is major girl and initially in the FIR and in the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
there was only allegation of harassment against the applicant but when the statement of the Vikas Viswakarma vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185839086/
1 prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she on the instigation of her father i.e.
informant of the case started making allegation of rape against the applicant.
5.

entities.text: Vikas Viswakarma vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that actually applicant and victim were having love affair but some dispute arose between both of them and thereafter father of the victim lodged FIR of the present case.
He next submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 18.04.2023.

6. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that prosecutrix of the case is major girl and victim did not make any allegation of rape against the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
7.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Although, victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant but there is no allegation of rape against the applicant either in the FIR or in the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and victim is major girl aged about 18 years.

9. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant - Vikas Viswakarma be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
